newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - June 19.

text.p: - There are 12 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- MING PAO said the future Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) government should not take any immediate and drastic changes on the labour policy. It said the new government should concentrate on increasing local workers' competitiveness, which was the fundamental reason for Hong Kong's economic development. It also suggested the future government set up an industrial district at the border, so that both Hong Kong and mainland workers could work there during the day, and go back to the environment they are familiar with after work.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said the draft of the Reunification Bill assured investors and the international community that although sovereignty changes after the handover, Hong Kong law-making and power-transfer will be carried out systematically, creating no chaos. It said Hong Kong's legal system would not be changed, its economic prosperity would be maintained, and investors' interests safeguarded. All who wish Hong Kong well would agree that the provisional legislature was a must after the through-train was destroyed by the British side, the paper said.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said that until Britain and China clarifed exactly what had happenedon during the border incident involving People's Liberation Army major-general Zhou Borong, speculation was bound to swirl around the incident. Undoubtedly there are more pressing issues on the Sino-British agenda, but this matter must be settled if the two sides wish to create an atmosphere of mutual trust.
